offence_severity: Minimum/Maximum: 302 IPC (death) - Minimum 7 years, Maximum 10 years or life imprisonment; 120B IPC (criminal conspiracy) - Minimum 6 months, Maximum 2 years; 34 IPC (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) - Minimum 1 year, Maximum 2 years
physical_harm: Death caused by torture during custodial interrogation
number_of_offences: Charged with 7 offences, 3 were finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The essence of the accusation is commission of custodial death owing to the torture to which victim-deceased was subjected to, from 17.07.1993 to 23.07.1993. There is absolute absence of any accusation or even an insinuation that the appellant had played any role in torturing victim.
witness_credibility: The statements of the witnesses recorded under Section 161, Cr.PC, including the witnesses related to the deceased Ram Kishore like Smt. Santosh, Shri Promod Kumar and Shri Bhim Singh, are taken as correct, but they would not reveal anything to base an allegation of criminal conspiracy or sharing of common intention against the appellant.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 15.07.1993; Trial judgment: 21.02.2000; High Court decision: 21.04.2023; Supreme Court decision: 15 July 2024
legal_representation: Siddhartha Dave, Sr. Adv., Ms. Pallavi Pratap, Ms. Prachi Pratap, Dr. Prashant Pratap, Akshay Singh, Gautam Mishra, Ms. Kinjal Aggarwal, Ms. Aakriti Priya, Ms. Muskan Jain, Advs. for the Appellant; Ardhendumauli Kumar Prasad, A.A.G., Sarvesh Singh Baghel, Abhinav S. Agarwal, Arun Pratap Singh Rajawat, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Dismissed application for discharge; High Court: Dismissed application under Section 482; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, set aside High Court and Trial Court orders
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant was involved in the custodial death of Ram Kishore through criminal conspiracy under Sections 120B and 34, IPC, and that the materials submitted by the prosecution supported this charge.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there was no material to arraign the appellant as an accused under Sections 120B and 34, IPC, and that the trial court's findings were based on suppositions and suspicions without foundational support from the prosecution's materials.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the Court must confine its consideration to the record of the case and the documents submitted therewith, and not base its findings on mere suppositions or suspicions.
precedent_relied_upon: State of Orissa v. Debendra Nath Padhi, P. Vijayan v. State of Kerala and Anr., Union of India v. Prafulla Kumar Samal, Yogesh alias Sachin Jagadish Joshi v. State of Maharashtra, State of Tamil Nadu v. N Suresh Rajan & Ors., R. Venkatakrishnan v. CBI, Ajay Aggarwal v. Union of India & Ors.
